Local Design Lab · closing gate

Design phase closed

The rail now names the participants, stage annotations are a two-slot contract rather than a layout builder, and View process has a home. Eight cards LOCKED, and a first implementation slice that needs no new backend work.

222px at 1–8 children8 cards LOCKED first slice: Attendance + Stafftypecheck rc=0

Participant identity bounded 222px at every count

Markers are avatar + first name via the existing CardAvatar primitive — the rail identifies the participant rather than abstracting them to initials, and no second avatar system appears.

ConditionTreatment
≤ 2 at a stageavatar + first name each
> 2two identities, then +N
Scoped participantalways individually visible, even where the stage would collapse
All at the case stageprojection suppressed; one muted line

A scoped child is never hidden behind a count — the operator asked about that child, so collapsing them would defeat the scope. Measured 222px at 1, 2, 3, 5 and 8 children: the rail does not grow, and the case marker never moves.

Stage annotations two slots, platform-capped

Platform ownsConfiguration owns
node anatomy · state treatment · case marker · marker placement · avatar and name treatment · selected emphasis · connectors · the two-line cap · typography · truncation · responsive · densitywhich canonical facts fill slot 1 and slot 2

No per-stage composition, no arbitrary schema, and no business truth stored in presentation configuration — a slot holds a projection of an authoritative fact. Proven across three processes with no domain branching: Enrollment Tour (Aug 27 · 10:00 AM / North Campus), Waitlist (#4 · Toddler / Joined Aug 19), Assignment Active (Sunflower Room / Mon–Fri), Billing Past due ($255 · 10 days / Visa declined Aug 16).

View process expanded density

The same card at density="expanded" — the centered Focus Card pattern already in use, not a standalone Process page.

P1 gates every historical fact

Entered, exited, outcome and transition render only when the canonical projection backs them; skipped and reopened are never inferred. With no projection the surface says so rather than drawing an empty timeline that reads like “nothing happened” — an operator cannot tell a guess from a record. P1 must not be solved in card state.

One card system — final composition

Spans chosen by the business question, not made uniform: Process and Attendance take the row, Financials 8/12 with a real 4/12 companion, the supporting cards 4/12, and the two person collections 6/12. Real runtime cards sit among the candidates without a seam.

Recommended first implementation slice

Attendance and Staff, read-only, registered. Both have complete canonical read truth today — ChildAttendanceReadModel, and employments + staff_presence_events + schedule_assignments — with no blocking gaps and no mutation dependency. They prove the entire registration path (provider, catalog, archetype, Surfaces placement) against cards whose truth already exists, before any card that needs new backend work.

Then: 2 F0 → F7 → F5 → Financials · 3 participant resolver → Process summary · 4 M1 → H1–H4 → Health · 5 P1 + G1 → expanded details · 6 S2 → S1 → Safety Signals.

Handoff — execution-ready mapping chains

Convergence plan §10 now carries all four chains — Financials, Process, Health, and Attendance / Staff / Care Team — with every line marked exists, partial or to build against a real module, table or registry. Plus the registration path each card follows once its read model lands, and the guard tests the implementation must carry:

GuardAsserts
Work View vs stageA lens cannot alter businessProcess.stageKey
Density invarianceChanging density changes no action's availability
Financial reconciliationgross − reductions − funding − payments = balance, on every specimen
Participant boundRail height is constant from 1 to N participants
Scoped visibilityA scoped participant is never collapsed into +N
History honestyNo entered/exited date renders without the P1 projection

Registration is per card, as its truth lands — never as a batch, and never ahead of the truth it projects.
